raw_case_text: A 24-year-old male was admitted in March 2014, with history of fever for 3 months. The fever was documented up to 103 F and was associated with sweating. There was history of insidious onset, progressive weakness of both lower limbs proximal more than distal in the form of not being able to stand from squatting, climbing up, and getting down stairs for the last 2 months. Simultaneously, he noticed proximal weakness in both upper limbs in the form of inability to lift heavy objects as he used to previously. Patient also gave history of difficulty in walking for the same duration. History of increased frequency of micturition accompanied with urgency and precipitancy was present for the last month. In addition patient had developed impairment in hearing for the last month. No history of headache, vomiting, ear discharge, altered sensorium, or seizures was reported. Review of other systems was normal. No significant past history was present. The patient belonged to a rural area and was associated with livestock rearing. He used to consume raw milk of goat. (This history was disclosed retrospectively.) On examination patient was febrile. Rest of the general physical examination was normal. On nervous system examination, our patient was conscious with the mini-mental state examination score of 28/30. Examination of cranial nerves revealed bilateral sensory neural deafness. Motor examination revealed normal muscle bulk, spasticity in upper and lower limbs, grade IV power in proximal muscles of both upper and lower limbs, symmetrically brisk deep tendon reflexes, and bilaterally extensor plantar response. Sensory examination was normal. Gait was spastic. No meningeal signs were present. Rest of the neurological examination was normal. Review of other systemic examinations was normal. On investigations hemoglobin was 11.6 gm% and total leukocyte count was 7200/cmm. Peripheral smear revealed a microcytic hypochromic picture. Biochemistry showed normal blood glucose and renal and liver functions. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis had proteins: 273 mg/dL; glucose: 29 mg/dL (concomitant blood glucose: 101 mg/dL); adenosine deaminase: 19.5 U/L. On microscopic examination of CSF total WBCs count was 288/cmm; neutrophils were 12%; lymphocytes were 88%; total RBCs count was 16/cmm. CSF was VDRL nonreactive, negative for cryptococcal infection and negative for acid fast bacilli by ZN stain. Chest X-ray and ultrasonography of abdomen were normal. As a part of fever workup his blood sample was sent to Department of Veterinary Microbiology, College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, CSK HPKV Palampur, Himachal Pradesh, for diagnosis of brucellosis. Blood sample was positive for RBT. SAT was positive in 1 : 640 titers. Subsequently brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was done. On T2W and FLAIR images white matter hyperintensities bilaterally involving periventricular white matter and centrum semiovale (mainly involving frontal lobes) with involvement of subcortical U fibres at places were observed. After contrast brainstem meningeal enhancement was seen (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). On pure tone audiometry bilateral moderate sensorineural hearing loss was documented. Patient was prescribed doxycycline 100 mg twice a day, rifampicin 600 mg once a day, and cotrimoxazole (160 mg trimethoprim and 800 mg sulfamethoxazole) twice a day. Patient became afebrile on fourth day of treatment. All three drugs were continued for three months. At the end of three months patient remained afebrile, deafness recovered, and bladder dysfunction and spastic gait improved. He had resumed his routine work. He faced difficulty only in running around. His upper motor neuron signs persisted on clinical examination. Repeat SAT titer was 1 : 160. So drugs were continued for another three months (total 6 months). Follow-up MRI at 6 months of treatment showed partial resolution of subcortical and periventricular white matter lesions in bilateral inferior frontal regions. Resolution of brainstem meningeal enhancement was also seen (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). Patient had a sequelae in the form of brisk deep tendon reflexes and bilaterally extensor plantar response after 6 months of therapy which was subsequently stopped. The functional status had a score of 1 on modified Rankin scale.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 24-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of high fever up to 103 °F with sweating, progressive bilateral limb weakness, difficulty walking, urinary urgency, and hearing impairment.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was admitted in March 2014 with a 3-month history of documented fever up to 103 °F associated with sweating. Over the last 2 months, he experienced insidious, progressive weakness of both lower limbs (proximal greater than distal, unable to stand from squatting or climb/descend stairs), proximal weakness of both upper limbs (inability to lift heavy objects), and difficulty walking. Over the preceding month, he developed increased urinary frequency with urgency and precipitancy, as well as bilateral hearing impairment. He had no history of headache, vomiting, ear discharge, altered sensorium, or seizures.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant past medical history. Epidemiological exposure: lived in a rural area, engaged in livestock rearing, and regularly consumed raw goat milk (disclosed retrospectively).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for urinary urgency, precipitancy, frequency, and hearing loss. Denied headache, vomiting, ear discharge, altered sensorium, or seizures; other systems normal. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Febrile on examination; rest of general physical examination normal. Neurological exam: conscious, MMSE 28/30. Cranial nerves: bilateral sensorineural deafness. Motor: normal muscle bulk, spasticity in upper and lower limbs, grade IV power in proximal muscles of bilateral upper and lower limbs, symmetrically brisk deep tendon reflexes, bilaterally extensor plantar responses. Sensory examination normal. Spastic gait. No meningeal signs. Other systemic examinations normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 11.6 gm%, total leukocyte count 7200/cmm; peripheral smear showed microcytic hypochromic picture. Normal blood glucose (concomitant blood glucose 101 mg/dL), normal renal and liver function tests. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasonography: normal. Pure tone audiometry: bilateral moderate sensorineural hearing loss.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture and CSF analysis: protein 273 mg/dL, glucose 29 mg/dL, adenosine deaminase (ADA) 19.5 U/L; CSF microscopy: total WBC count 288/cmm (12% neutrophils, 88% lymphocytes), total RBC count 16/cmm; CSF VDRL nonreactive, negative for cryptococcal infection, and negative for acid-fast bacilli by ZN stain. Brain MRI: T2W and FLAIR white matter hyperintensities bilaterally involving periventricular white matter and centrum semiovale (predominantly frontal lobes) with involvement of subcortical U fibers; post-contrast brainstem meningeal enhancement. Follow-up brain MRI at 6 months showed partial resolution of subcortical and periventricular white matter lesions in bilateral inferior frontal regions and resolution of brainstem meningeal enhancement.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Neurobrucellosis presenting with meningoencephalomyelitis and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Confirmed by positive Rose Bengal test (RBT) and serum agglutination test (SAT) positive at 1 : 640 titer (titer decreased to 1 : 160 at 3 months). Neurosyphilis, cryptococcosis, and tuberculosis excluded. Treatment & Outcome: Prescribed doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, rifampicin 600 mg once daily, and cotrimoxazole (trimethoprim 160 mg / sulfamethoxazole 800 mg) twice daily for 6 months. Patient became afebrile on day 4 of treatment. At 3 months, hearing recovered, bladder dysfunction and spastic gait improved, and he resumed work. At 6 months, therapy was discontinued with residual brisk deep tendon reflexes and bilaterally extensor plantars (modified Rankin scale score of 1).
